newsitem.title: UK: EU seen awarding up to 60,000 t sugar at tender.
newsitem.headline: EU seen awarding up to 60,000 t sugar at tender.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is expected to award up to 60,000 tonnes of current series white sugar at its weekly tender later on Wednesday, traders said.
But a level nearer 30,000 tonnes was more likely as there was little urgent requirement at present for export licences, they said.
"I think it'll be another limited tonnage as there's a lot more "C" sugar in the system," said one.
"The producers have adopted a tactic of disposing of that before they start looking at the tenders and that still seems to be going on," he said.

This week's restitution award is expected to be based on the Matif May futures contract as March expires next week. The maximum restitution level was estimated at 45.518 Ecus (European currency units).
But another trader was more cautious and said a low tonnage was likely for this week's award.
"If they do give May I still don't think the tonnage will be wonderful," he said.
"I think we'd be looking at 30,000 tonnes maximum and I wouldn't be surprised if we went down to as low as last week again."
Last week the EU awarded 14,250 tonnes of white sugar with maximum export rebate set at 45.422 Ecus. Licences are currently valid until the end of July.
But the low tonnage awards are not helping the EU keep on track with its sugar export programme, traders said.
"Sugar is disappearing and there aren't vast stocks overhanging the market," said the first trader.
"But obviously the Commission would like to catch up on its schedule to make sure they're not left with unacceptably high stocks at the end of the year."
